title: Yes, We Trust the Day Is Breaking
description: Yes, We Trust the Day Is Breaking in Tonic Solfa to ST. AUSTIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Kelly wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 299 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Encouraging Prospects”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked 8.7.8.7.4.7, to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AUSTIN; any other 8.7.8.7.4.7 tune fits them as well.
underlay: Yes, we trust the day is break-ing; Joy-ful times are near at hand; God, the might-y God, is speak-ing, By his word, in ev-ery land: When he choos-es, Dark-ness flies at his com-mand.

lines: Yes, we trust the day is breaking;
Joyful times are near at hand;
God, the mighty God, is speaking,
By his word, in every land:
While the foe becomes more daring,
While he enters like a flood,
Means to spread his truth abroad:
Soon shall tell the love of God.
God of Jacob, high and glorious,
Let thy people see thy hand;
Through the world, in every land;

licence: Public domain: Thomas Kelly died in 1855.
credits: Words by Thomas Kelly (1769–1855), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AUSTIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
